subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is Tom from <Picture 1>. The front, back, side, and close-up views in <Picture 1> are alternate identity views of the same single physical character, not separate characters. Preserve Tom's blue-gray fur, white muzzle and belly, large pink inner ears, yellow-green eyes, black eyebrows, small black nose, white gloves, white lower legs and feet, and blue-gray tail with a white tip. Preserve the flat graphic proportions and recognizable cartoon design of the reference sheet.
<Video 1> is the source video. It provides the original first eight seconds of body movement, facial-expression timing, camera framing, background, lighting, pacing, and spatial composition.
<Audio 1> is the original synchronized audio from the first eight seconds of <Video 1>, retained unchanged.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation + audio reuse] The target video is the first eight seconds of <Video 1> with the original performer replaced by exactly one Tom character from <Picture 1>. Preserve everything else: the original background, lakeside environment, mountain, lighting, camera angle, framing, motion speed, timing, body trajectory, foot placement, sound, and overall visual composition. Transfer the performer's exact movement and expression timing to Tom's cartoon facial controls and body animation.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (visible throughout the first eight seconds): attribute_transfer - Tom's identity, cartoon anatomy, colors, facial design, gloves, feet, and tail are transferred onto the original performer's exact body movement, pose sequence, gaze direction, head turns, weight shifts, and expression timing.
<Picture 1> (Tom identity reference): fully_preserved - preserve the character's recognizable design, head proportions, ear shape, eye shape, muzzle, colors, gloves, feet, and tail markings.
<Video 1> (motion, camera, environment, and composition source): fully_preserved - preserve the original first eight seconds, including background, camera, lighting, body choreography, movement rhythm, framing, and scene continuity.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy - reuse the original first eight seconds of synchronized audio without changes.

detailed_description:
The target video is a vertical 9:16 character-replacement edit. Preserve the original outdoor lakeside setting, gray paved ground, distant trees, large rocky mountain, pale overcast daylight, camera distance, camera angle, framing, and background composition exactly as shown in <Video 1>. Do not add new scenery, props, camera moves, zooms, cuts, transitions, music, or sound effects.

Replace the original performer with exactly one instance of <Subject 1>, rendered as a stylized cartoon Tom with clean cel-shaded graphic rendering that preserves the visual design of <Picture 1>. Do not turn Tom into a realistic human, a generic cat, or a different cartoon style.

Exactly one instance of <Subject 1> is visible throughout the video. <Subject 1> remains one single physical character with one continuous complete body. No duplicate, clone, twin, doppelganger, extra copy, lookalike, ghost image, afterimage, motion trail, split body, or suddenly appearing extra character.

From 00:00.000 to 00:08.000, reproduce the source performer’s complete movement continuously and in exact temporal order. Preserve every visible action: the initial diagonal stance, knee bending, changes in leg width, lateral weight shifts, torso inclination, shoulder rotation, arm raises, arm sweeps, wrist rotations, finger openings, hand height, elbow angles, head turns, gaze direction, and final pose. Preserve the original foot positions and stepping trajectory, but replace the human shoes with Tom’s white cartoon feet.

Transfer the source performer’s facial-expression timing into Tom’s cartoon facial controls. Match the exact timing and intensity of eyebrow movement, eye openness, pupil direction, eyelid changes, head orientation, muzzle tension, and mouth shape. Keep Tom’s yellow-green eyes, black eyebrows, white muzzle, and black nose consistently recognizable. Do not invent new smiles, speech, exaggerated blinking, lip-sync, or emotional reactions that are absent from the source video.

Maintain the original performer’s screen position, body scale, silhouette, motion speed, rhythm, and relationship to the background at every moment. Tom’s tail follows his body balance naturally and remains visually consistent with the reference design without creating extra motion that is not present in the source performance.

End exactly at 00:08.000 on the source video’s corresponding pose and facial state.

overall_soundscape:
Reuse <Audio 1> unchanged for the first eight seconds, including the original ambience, music, environmental sound, and movement-related sound. Keep the audio synchronized with the preserved motion. Do not add dialogue or new sound effects.

non_diegetic_music:
Preserve only the music already present in <Audio 1>. Do not add or modify background music.
